steps.caption: APODICTIC reads your manuscript before it hears your plans.
From the text alone it predicts the contract: genre, the promise to readers, and the controlling idea.
It measures the book against that contract, with passes calibrated to the genre. A slow opening is fine in literary fiction and a defect in a thriller.
It also sets the prediction beside the contract you meant to write.
Where they differ, that mismatch is the diagnosis: the text is not communicating what you think it is.
Everything feeds the editorial letter, which names classes of solution and never rewrites your prose. Argument pieces get the same check against claim, audience, burden and stakes.
